lesson_title: Magnetism: The Pole You Can Never Cut Off
hook_text: Cut a magnet in half to keep just the north pole. Congratulations — you now own TWO complete magnets. Try again forever; you'll always fail.
clip_script: Take a magnetised pin: north at the tip, south at the eye. Snip it in the middle to keep just the north half. Test your half-pin — and it has a brand-new south end at the cut. Snip again: same story. Grind it to powder and every speck is still a complete little magnet, two poles each. Why? A magnet is not north substance glued to south substance. Inside, countless tiny fields have lined up, all facing the same way, like a stadium crowd doing the same wave. Cut the crowd in half and each half is still doing the wave. There was never a north half to keep.
visual_style: A pin snipped again and again, each fragment sprouting fresh N and S labels; zoom inside to a stadium crowd of arrows doing the wave, split down the middle, both halves still waving.
pacing: Rapid snip-snip-snip escalation, pause on the powder, slow zoom into the crowd of arrows for the payoff.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — and find out why the Arctic hides a magnetic SOUTH pole.
